title: Unit – 1 : Session – 1 : SLO – 1  |  Functional units of a computer
sections: 1. C — To design better programs and optimize performance
1. TRUE — The system software level (OS) handles memory protection and process synchronization.
2. FALSE — Cache memory is faster (and smaller) than RAM.
3. FALSE — Machine-level programs execute directly; compilers are needed for high-level languages.
4. TRUE — Harvard architecture uses separate buses for instructions and data.
5. FALSE — Control units can be hardwired or microprogrammed.
Suggested change: Move from pure von Neumann architecture to a Harvard / modified-Harvard architecture with separate instruction and data buses (and add cache memory plus more RAM).

Why: In von Neumann architecture a single shared bus forces instruction fetches and data transfers to take turns, creating the von Neumann bottleneck. Separate buses let the CPU fetch instructions and read/write data simultaneously, and cache reduces trips to the slow main memory. Together these remove the memory lags and raise throughput without changing the programs themselves.
